text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":0.5},"rationale":"Seven evaluated points plateau at 156.32-157.64us with identical 34.603MB simulator DRAM traffic regardless of tile, stages, or swizzle, so the serpentine-reuse traffic hypothesis remains unconfirmed and traffic stays at weight 1 with no reward; swizzle stays open but is non-discriminating (attempts 01-03 identical at same tile/stages; 05 vs 06 identical across swizzle 16 vs 8). Best remains attempt-04 (block_M=32, block_N=128, block_K=64, stages=1, swizzle=16) at 156.32us with 20480B smem and 4 blocks/SM; attempt-05/06 (block_M=64) regressed to 157.64us at 32768B and 3 blocks/SM, supporting the low-smem/high-occupancy direction. However, footprint weight 0.1 in attempt-06 over-penalized smem and steered the solver away from the incumbent neighborhood into a repeat of block_M=64, so I raise footprint to 0.5 to keep a mild preference for low-smem/high-occupancy candidates without discarding the incumbent's block_M=32 corner. Pipeline stays 1 (stages=1 has produced the two best points), launches stays 1, traffic stays 1 but is not raised given flat simulator traffic. Domains stay broad: only seven tuples excluded and the 32768-byte portability cap still admits many combos (tightest BM=128,BN=128,BK=64,stages=2). Next hypothesis: probe untested low-smem corners near the incumbent with block_M=32/block_N=64/block_K=32/stages=1-2 and block_M=32/block_N=128/block_K=32/stages=1 across swizzle values, checking whether higher blocks/SM breaks the ~156us plateau; if swizzle still shows no simulator traffic/latency effect, collapse it later. Proxy cost is dimensionless ranking only, never microseconds; Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR but not the CUDA binary; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed."}
